item.title: St. Charles County unveils 785-acre wetland park for birds
item.description: The Jay and Caroline Henges Wetland Park and Education Center is opening in St. Charles County as the newest and largest park in the county. The 785-acre site is a hybrid wildlife area designed to protect critical habitat for birds traveling along the national flyway.

item.title: Jefferson County hosts event on drug and alcohol education
item.description: Law enforcement and community organizations in Jefferson County held an event tonight in Cedar Hill to raise awareness about drug and alcohol abuse. The seminar focused on educating parents about the warning signs of addiction and connecting families with local recovery resources.

item.title: Missouri psychiatrist settles $360K false billing case
item.description: A Missouri psychiatrist has agreed to pay $360,000 to resolve allegations she falsely billed federal and state health programs for psychotherapy services she did not provide, federal prosecutors announced Monday.

item.title: St. Charles County to decide on church-to-sports club plan
item.description: County leaders in St. Charles are scheduled to vote later this month on a proposal to convert a former church and gym into a private youth sports club.

item.title: Detective testifies against former cops in civil rights trial
item.description: A police detective has testified for days in the federal case against two former Northwoods, MO officers charged in a kidnapping/assault case.

item.title: Debate continues in Festus on proposed data center
item.description: Although the proposed data center was not on the agenda during Monday night’s regular Festus City Council meeting, it remains a major topic of conversation across the city.

item.title: Citizen-led testing in Cahokia Heights detects E. coli in drinking water
item.description: A citizen-led effort to test drinking water in Cahokia Heights has renewed residents’ concerns after some samples tested positive for E. coli.

item.title: Two St. Louis rappers shot and killed in four-day span
item.description: Surveillance video captured a burst of gunfire in an alley just off Arsenal Street on March 4, leaving a 20-year-old man dead and raising concerns of possible retaliation and escalating community violence.

item.title: St. Louis mattress company accused of unresolved complaints, BBB says
item.description: The Better Business Bureau is warning customers of a St. Louis-based mattress company based on several "unanswered and unresolved complaints."

item.title: Former Missouri House speaker sentenced to prison for COVID relief fraud
item.description: A former top Missouri lawmaker has been sentenced to 21 months in prison for misusing pandemic relief funds. Former Republican state House Speaker John Diehl pleaded guilty to wire fraud for using about $380,000 of federal loans on personal expenses instead of his law firm's operating costs.
